reason: The exact v19 batch-5 pilot produced only 56.7% post-type exact sets on 30 English development rows, while product labels, outcomes, and sentiment remained strong. This last bounded batch-isolation test retains the byte-exact base prompt, production parser, fallback, repair, model, and temperature but supplies one post per request. It determines whether any batch peers cause the common-type ceiling. It cannot approve release.

cohort.selection: the same frozen 30 EN rows used by v19; no row or label selection changed after scoring

production_shape_under_test.all_other_runtime_behavior: byte-exact v18 base prompt and existing strict parser, fallback, repair allowance, and telemetry

decision_rule: Continue this base-prompt architecture only if all 30 rows validate, EN exact post-type sets are at least 0.70, exact product-label sets are at least 0.85, outcome accuracy is at least 0.90, and every supported post/product label meets its unchanged floor. A pass permits an all-locale development probe; it does not approve release. A failure rejects further batch-size tuning of this all-in-one base prompt and requires a different decomposed classification task before more transport.
global_stop: The client reserves the current request's conservative input estimate, full output allowance, transport attempt, and maximum price before network transport. It refuses the first operation that would exceed any cap. Cached successful responses replay without new reservations, and capacity cannot transfer to another cohort, model, prompt, batch size, or lane.
